issues.title: Define Agent Identity, Agent Identifier, and Agent Description in Terminology
issues.author: sinakhatibi
issues.body:
### Problem
The document defines key concepts (e.g., AI Agent, Session, Task) but does not define the identity-related terminology needed for interoperability: **Agent Identity**, **Agent Identifier**, and (implicitly) the agent self-description object used for discovery/interoperability.

At the same time, identity concepts are already assumed by multiple requirements:
- **CMN-1** (mutual authentication)
- **B3-2** (identity preservation across multi-hop delegation)
- **B3-6** (agent identifier format resolvable to endpoint)

Without explicit definitions:
- It is unclear what exactly is being authenticated (identity vs endpoint vs credentials).
- Implementations may diverge in how identity is represented and scoped.
- The relationship between identity, identifiers, credentials, and endpoint resolution remains ambiguous.
- This creates interoperability and security inconsistencies across deployments.

### Proposed Change
Add the following definitions to the **Terminology** section (minimal, non-prescriptive):

- **Agent Identity**: a persistent or temporary identifier associated with an AI agent, used for authentication, authorization, and accountability.
- **Agent Identifier**: a structured representation of an agent identity that may be resolvable to a network endpoint and bound to cryptographic credentials.
- **Agent Description**: a structured representation of an agent’s identity, capabilities, endpoints, security requirements, and metadata, used for discovery and interoperability.

### Acceptance Criteria
- The Terminology section includes the above three definitions.
- Existing requirements referencing authentication, identity preservation, and identifier format (CMN-1, B3-2, B3-6) can be interpreted consistently without changing their meaning.
``

pulls.title: Sina-batch-01 - Add missing terminology
pulls.author: sinakhatibi
pulls.body:
## Summary
This PR expands and clarifies the **Terminology** section to remove ambiguity around agent identity and to define core protocol primitives used throughout the draft (tasks, sessions, messages, discovery, and capability semantics). 

The changes are split across multiple small commits (one term per commit) to make review easier.

## Motivation
The draft previously defined only a minimal terminology set (e.g., AI Agent, Orchestrator Agent, Tool, Mediator Agent, Session, Task, etc.).   
However, identity is already assumed by requirements such as **CMN-1** (mutual authentication) and multi-hop delegation requirements such as **B3-2** and **B3-6**, without explicit definitions of what “agent identity” and “agent identifier” mean. This can lead to divergent interpretations and interoperability/security inconsistencies. [1](https://nokia.sharepoint.com/sites/gxp/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BBBA4E6A4-9EF8-47F2-BFD0-DD97EC8BFB77%7D&file=6G%20Network%20for%20AI%20agent%20in%20terminal.pptx&action=edit&mobileredirect=true)

## What changed
### Added terminology (new terms)
- **User**
- **Agent Identity**, **Agent Identifier**, **Agent Description**
- **Message**, **Context**, **Event**, **Artifact**
- **Capability**
- **Delegation**, **Task Execution Context**, **Task State**
- **Correlation Identifier**
- **Worker Agent** and **Tool Agent** (as role-compatible aliases)

### Clarified existing terminology
- **Tool**: clarified that a tool is not necessarily an agent and may not participate in A2A communication.
- **Session**: clarified relationship between session and context (session may carry/maintain contexts).
- **Task**: expanded definition to include identifier, structure (inputs/outputs), and async/progress/result semantics.
- **Coordinator Agent**: clarified that agents may assume multiple roles depending on interaction context.

## Scope / Non-goals
- Terminology-only update: no changes to protocol requirements, no new protocol mechanisms introduced.
- Does not prescribe a specific identity provisioning framework; it defines terms to make existing requirements interpretable consistently.

## Issue linkage
Closes #38 [1](https://nokia.sharepoint.com/sites/gxp/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BBBA4E6A4-9EF8-47F2-BFD0-DD97EC8BFB77%7D&file=6G%20Network%20for%20AI%20agent%20in%20terminal.pptx&action=edit&mobileredirect=true)

## Notes for reviewers
Commits are intentionally small (one term per commit) to keep discussions isolated and allow selective revert if needed. I can squash after review if preferred.

pulls.title: Refine agent identifier format requirement in draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements.md to clarify its uniqueness and resolution to communication endpoints.
pulls.author: sinakhatibi
pulls.body:
## Summary
This PR clarifies requirement **B3-6** to avoid conflating **agent identity** with **network location** by allowing agent identifier resolution to occur **directly or indirectly** via an appropriate discovery mechanism. [2](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/details?eventId=AAMkAGYzMjEzYzkwLTczYzAtNGNiMS1iNmUxLTUzNjk5MDYwNTAwYQBGAAAAAACR_t3-pC1iQI99yygrBPqXBwB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAAAAAENAAB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAcfHH4mAAA%3d)

## Motivation / Problem
Issue #41 highlights that the current wording of **B3-6** (“agent identifier format resolvable to the agent’s endpoint”) can be interpreted as tightly binding an identifier to a specific endpoint/location. This:
- conflates logical identity with network location,
- over-constrains architecture choices, and
- makes it harder to support registry-based or privacy-preserving deployment models. [1](https://github.com/tireddy2/agentic-ai-ucreq2/issues/41)[2](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/details?eventId=AAMkAGYzMjEzYzkwLTczYzAtNGNiMS1iNmUxLTUzNjk5MDYwNTAwYQBGAAAAAACR_t3-pC1iQI99yygrBPqXBwB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAAAAAENAAB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAcfHH4mAAA%3d)

## What changed
### Before
B3-6 required an agent identifier format “resolvable to the agent’s endpoint using an appropriate discovery mechanism.” [2](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/details?eventId=AAMkAGYzMjEzYzkwLTczYzAtNGNiMS1iNmUxLTUzNjk5MDYwNTAwYQBGAAAAAACR_t3-pC1iQI99yygrBPqXBwB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAAAAAENAAB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAcfHH4mAAA%3d)

### After (proposed)
B3-6 is revised to state that an agent identifier:
- uniquely represents an agent identity, and
- can be resolved **directly or indirectly** to the agent’s communication endpoint using an appropriate discovery mechanism.

The key clarification is **“directly or indirectly”**, which preserves the original intent (identifiers must be resolvable) while explicitly permitting indirection via registries, mediators, directories, or other discovery deployments. [1](https://github.com/tireddy2/agentic-ai-ucreq2/issues/41)[2](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/details?eventId=AAMkAGYzMjEzYzkwLTczYzAtNGNiMS1iNmUxLTUzNjk5MDYwNTAwYQBGAAAAAACR_t3-pC1iQI99yygrBPqXBwB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAAAAAENAAB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAcfHH4mAAA%3d)

## Scope / Non-goals
- This is a **requirements wording clarification only**.
- It does **not** introduce or mandate a particular discovery protocol, registry API, or privacy mechanism.
- It does **not** change the requirement that a discovery mechanism is needed; it only avoids over-constraining how resolution is achieved. [2](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/details?eventId=AAMkAGYzMjEzYzkwLTczYzAtNGNiMS1iNmUxLTUzNjk5MDYwNTAwYQBGAAAAAACR_t3-pC1iQI99yygrBPqXBwB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAAAAAENAAB5wvnpV8qJT4-SrFbv9aLGAAcfHH4mAAA%3d)

## Issue linkage
Closes #41 [1](https://github.com/tireddy2/agentic-ai-ucreq2/issues/41)

pulls.title: Add AGTP to related work references
pulls.author: hoodchris
pulls.body:
Add AGTP to the related work references in Section 1.

The AGTP (Agent Transfer Protocol) draft family is relevant adjacent work to this requirements document. AGTP addresses a substantial subset of the requirements catalogued here (CMN-1, CMN-2, CMN-4, CMN-7; B3-1 through B3-8; B5-2; A1-1 through A1-9) through a dedicated agent-native protocol substrate rather than HTTP-based extensions.

Draft family: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-hood-independent-agtp/
Reference implementation: https://github.com/nomoticai/agtp
Full suite specifications: https://agtp.io

Including AGTP in the related work catalog makes the document more complete for readers evaluating the agent infrastructure landscape, regardless of which architectural approach the resulting WG pursues.
